notes: Corrected twice against the earlier alignment. (1) The copula moves from the `כְּ` to `נַהַם`: the Hebrew predicate is the noun and the comparative phrase modifies it, which is exactly the adjunct case rule 49's closing paragraph carves out. (2) The assimilated article becomes `unrepresented` and the written *the* becomes `נַהַם`'s supplied determiner, because the ASV writes *a lion* before the article's own word and rule 29 forbids fronting where the rectum carries a determiner of its own.
Both marginal notes (*Or, angereth himself against him*; *Hebrew soul*) were read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).
